out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed the handsink to the right of the 2 vat prep sink being used to store food container and lids for to go containers.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT HAND SINKS CAN ONLY BE USED FOR WASHING HANDS. PIC REMOVED THE CONTAINER AND LIDS FROM THE HAND WASHING SINK.

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. PIC WAS ABLE TO PROVIDE HAND SOAP FOR EACH HAND WASHING SINK AT TIME OF INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Durable Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not resistant to corrosion: facility is using home storage containers to store food items.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL CONTAINERS MUST BE FOOD SAFE IN ORDER TO STORE FOOD. PLEASE GET RID OF ALL HOME USE STORAGE CONTAINERS BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 41F, No More than 6 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours. GRILLED PORK WAS TEMPING AT 52F OVER 12 AFTER BEING COOKED. PIC WAS ABLE TO SHOW PROOF THAT PORK COOLED PROPERLY.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours and to 41F within a total of six hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THE CORRECT COOLING PARAMETERS FOR FOODS. PIC THREW AWAY PORK THAT WAS NOT TEMPING PROPERLY.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Cooked chicken was temping at 51F in the 2DR prep top unit.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC TOLD EHS THE CHICKEN WAS COOKED THE DAY PRIOR AND HAD BEEN REMOVED FROM WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR THIS MORNING. THE CHICKEN HAD BEEN IN THE PREP TOP UNIT FOR 1 HOUR, PIC MOVED THE CHICKEN BACK TO THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR TO RAPIDLY COOL TO 41F OR BELOW.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: MULTIPLE PIECES OF GRILLED PORK WERE COOLING IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR IN A SMALL CONTAINER WHERE ALL THE PORK WAS STACKED ON TOP OF ONE ANOTHER, AND HEAT WAS NOT ABLE TO ESCAPE. THE PORK WAS UNABLE TO COOL PROPERLY.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC WAYS TO FACILITATE PROPER COOLING OF COOKED FOOD ITEMS. PIC THREW AWAY THE PORK THAT WAS NOT TEMPING PROPERLY.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Manufacturer containers were observed reused for the storage of multiple food items throughout the facility.
violations.corrective_action: Manufacturer containers may not be reused for secondary storage of other foods because the containers are not durable enough for multiple reuse and become uncleanable. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THE CONTAINERS THAT ARE ALLOWED TO BE USED FOR FOOD STORAGE AND WHAT TO LOOK FOR WHEN BUYING NEW FOOD SAFE CONTAINERS. PIC AGREED TO BUY NEW FOOD SAFE CONTAINERS BY TIME OF NEXT INSPECTION.

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. EHS WITNESSED AN EMPLOYEE PICK UP MINCED GARLIC OFF KITCHEN FLOOR WITH BARE HANDS AND DID NOT WASH HANDS BEFORE ATTEMPTING TO BEGIN COOKING AGAIN.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS EXPLAINED TO THE PIC WHY FOOD CAN NEVER BE PREPARED AFTER TOUCHING THE FLOOR WITH BARE HANDS OR GLOVED HANDS. PIC MADE EMPLOYEE WASH HANDS BEFORE BEGINNING TO PREP FOOD AGAIN.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Access to Handwashing Sink
violations.observation: The handwashing facility located to the left of a 2 vat prep sink is blocked by prepped food and storage buckets, preventing access by employees for easy handwashing.
violations.corrective_action: A hand washing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use. PIC THREW AWAY FOOD THAT WAS IN THE HAND SINK AND MOVED THE STORAGE BUCKETS OUT OF THE WAY.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: COOKED SHRIMP, SAUSAGE AND CHICKEN SPRING ROLLS WERE BEING STORED TOGETHER IN ONE CONTAINER IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. PIC THREW AWAY SHRIMP, SAUSAGE AND CHICKEN SPRING ROLLS THAT WERE ALL BE STORED TOGETHER IN THE SAME CONTAINER. EHS DISCUSSED THAT DUE TO THE SHRIMP BEING AN ALLERGEN, IT MUST ALL BE THROWN AWAY.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: SCOOPS WITHOUT HANDLES ARE BEING USED IN LARGE BULK STORAGE CONTAINERS.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL SCOOPS MEED TP HAVE HANDLES ON THEM AND THEY NEED TO BE STORED WITH THE HANDLE UP TO PREVENT CONTAMINATION. PIC GET NEW SCOOPS WITH HANDLES BY NEXT INSPECTION.
